blockers.verbatim_goal: Prove tpOf_stabFree_eq_of_splice: given hg : IsLadderPath, a pending region at a, an object cycle of length l with l | P + 1 inside it, a spliced ladder path g' supplied as a hypothesis, and Tc <= |a - z| with hp : ParamsOk, the stab-free part of tpOf at z is the same along both.
blockers.what_was_tried: The uniform-claim structural induction (refuted at the seam by the compiled spliceIdx_seam_lt, dispatch seq 17), then the preceding round's two intelligence items: a distance budget per U/S-nesting depth together with the splice's monotonicity on future object positions. The budget item was pursued to its conclusion and then abandoned in favour of compiling the counterexample it predicts.
blockers.why_it_failed: The statement is false. One splice duplicates the pumped block, so it adds one occurrence of every object state of that block to the walk's future, and a nested eventuality counts occurrences at unbounded distance — so the distance hypothesis Tc <= |a - z| buys nothing. On a three-state object whose walk hits the p-state exactly once, the nesting-depth-three formula (top U (p AND top U p)) is false along the original at every position and true along the spliced path. Compiled as Probe761S.splice_type_invariance_refuted, and it survives the (P + 1) / l iterations the residue coordinate of kappa needs (twoHits_iterate, spliced_rehypotheses).
